core_obligations: Embed F into an injective I, which has trivial higher Cech cohomology, and form the quotient Q (proof lines 1650-1658).
Use the hypothesis to see that the short exact sequence is exact as a sequence of presheaves, so that the long exact Cech sequence gives the Cech vanishing of Q as well (proof lines 1659-1665).

Run the long exact cohomology sequence: H^n(U, I) = 0 for n > 0 and surjectivity on H^0 gives H^1(U, F) = 0; the same step applied to Q gives H^2(U, F) = 0, and the argument repeats (proof lines 1668-1692).
proof_roadmap: Injective resolution and the resulting quotient (proof lines 1650-1658).
Exactness of presheaves and Cech vanishing of the quotient (proof lines 1659-1665).
Induction on the degree via the long exact sequence (proof lines 1668-1692).
difficulty_reason: For a module F on a ringed space whose Cech cohomology vanishes in positive degrees for every open covering of every open, the lemma concludes the vanishing of ordinary cohomology in positive degrees on every open (statement lines 1630-1644). The proof embeds F into an injective I, uses that injectives have trivial higher Cech cohomology, and observes that the short exact sequence then remains exact as a sequence of presheaves by the hypothesis, so that the quotient Q inherits the Cech vanishing (proof lines 1647-1665). The long exact cohomology sequence then gives the vanishing by induction: H^n(U, I) = 0 for n > 0 makes H^1(U, F) vanish, the same argument applied to Q gives H^1(U, Q) = 0 and hence H^2(U, F) = 0, and the argument repeats (proof lines 1668-1692). The claim is H2: a standard injective-and-induct argument whose only non-formal step is the recognition that the hypothesis makes the sequence of presheaves exact.
